headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from cognee’s session-memory, document-ingesting support role paired with a local-only game agent; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents and maintains session memory, so if godot_rl_agents consumes its outputs through a shared workspace or manual handoff, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair has no documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are copied into a workspace that godot_rl_agents reads as instructions
IF either agent treats file content as trusted without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a provenance header to any handoff file
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data, but godot_rl_agents has no data classes, no network egress, and no shared workspace or OAuth surface is documented. That makes leakage plausible only through unusual operator bridging, with small blast radius in the documented pair.
conditions: IF the operator copies sensitive cognee outputs into godot_rl_agents inputs
IF a shared filesystem is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep sensitive outputs out of the game agent’s workspace
Use redacted samples for any cross-agent testing
Delete copied artifacts after review
Restrict cognee outputs to non-sensitive test data
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee has allowlisted network egress and session-scoped memory, while godot_rl_agents has no documented write, network, git, or OAuth capabilities. With no overlapping mutable surface in the profiles, a write conflict is not plausible from the documented pair.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents is later given write access to the same directory as cognee
IF either profile gains shared mutable resources not shown here
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate filesystems
Avoid granting write access to shared repos
Review any future capability changes before pairing
Use read-only exports for cross-agent exchange

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee can produce decisions, workflows, and schema structures that a downstream agent might reuse, but godot_rl_agents is a game-playing agent with no documented action-taking authority. The pathway exists only if an operator feeds cognee output into the game agent as authoritative input, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are treated as authoritative by a downstream controller
IF godot_rl_agents is used to act on those outputs without verification
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents
Label cognee outputs as untrusted suggestions
Use schema validation on all handoffs
Limit downstream actions to simulation only
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while godot_rl_agents has no documented compliance controls, residency, or retention policy. Because the pair lacks evidence of matching safeguards, any regulated-data handoff creates a compliance mismatch risk even though the second agent is local-only.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from cognee is forwarded into godot_rl_agents logs or artifacts
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared data class
mitigations: Do not forward regulated data into the game agent
Redact personal and finance fields before handoff
Set short retention on any shared artifacts
Document the data flow and retention owner
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
